audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: The catalog codes Kwoma as fixed-dominant initial stress on the strength of a Wikipedia sentence with an empty cite/loc/grade. The primary source behind that sentence, Kooyers, Kooyers & Bee 1971 (Te Reo 14), was downloaded from the Linguistic Society of New Zealand's open archive and scanned: p. 41, section 4, states verbatim "Non-phonemic stress falls on the initial syllable of each word." This confirms the classification (fixed initial, non-contrastive) and should replace Wikipedia as the deciding citation, with locator 'p. 41, sec. 4 Distribution' and an upgraded strength of the evidence (primary phonology article by the SIL fieldworkers, 1961-66 fieldwork). Kooyers 1974 (held pp. 9-74 via Rosetta Project) and Bowden 1997 (held, ANU open access) are silent on word stress and defer to the 1971 article. No better or later stress description exists per Glottolog (2 descriptive refs) and the indexes queried, s
audit.second_reader_evidence: Independent re-check of confirms every finding of the prior first reader. (1) Catalog record: classification fixed-dominant, rule initial (initial stress), cite/loc/grade empty, sole source = English Wikipedia 'Kwoma language' ("Stress occurs on the first syllable of words."); catalog unit shows the strength of the evidence 'carried-secondary', in the dominant set, not in the strict set under the 2026-08-31 an earlier compilation owner ruling 'dominant set only at an earlier compilation grade; STRICT entry stays deep-note-gated'. (2) Wikipedia: saved wikitext line 38 carries the sentence verbatim inside the (unreferenced) consonants paragraph -- quote chec

sources.citation: Kooyers, Orneal, Martha Kooyers & Darlene Bee. 1971. The phonemes of Washkuk (Kwoma). Te Reo 14: 36-41. Open copy:https://nzlingsoc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Kooyers-Bee-1971.pdf(image-only PDF; scanned one page at a time, 300 dpi).
sources.quote: "Each word consists of either a single syllable (either CV or CVC) or a sequence of CV syllables with or without a final CVC syllable. ... Non-phonemic stress falls on the initial syllable of each word."
sources.locator: p. 41, section 4 'Distribution' (scanned text: line 231; page scan verified visually)
